name: OKLCh
author: Björn Ottosson
description: Cylindrical form of OKLab. L = perceptual lightness, C = chroma (colorfulness), h = hue angle in degrees. The most useful space for generative color work: rotate h to change hue, scale C to desaturate, adjust L to change brightness — all perceptually uniform.

L.name: Lightness
L.notes: 0 = black, 1 = white. Perceptually linear — same as OKLab L.

C.name: Chroma
C.notes: 0 = achromatic (gray), ~0.4 = maximally saturated (varies by hue and L). Not normalized — actual maximum depends on hue and lightness.

h.name: Hue angle
h.note: OKLCh hue angles do NOT match HSL hue angles. Yellow is ~109°, not 60°.

relationship_to_oklab.h_formula: h = atan2(b, a) × 180 / π, normalized to [0, 360)

conversion_chain.to_srgb: OKLCh → OKLab → linear sRGB → gamma encode → sRGB

use_cases: Hue rotation that preserves perceived brightness and saturation
Generating harmony angles that look evenly spaced to the eye
Chroma manipulation — fade to gray without changing hue or lightness
Palette generation with equal perceptual spacing
Gamut mapping (reduce C until color fits in sRGB)
Animated color cycling with stable lightness
known_issues: Hue angles don't correspond to HSL hue angles — yellow is ~109°, not 60°
Maximum chroma varies by hue and lightness — no single safe chroma value
Gamut mapping required before converting to sRGB for high-chroma values
Not standardized by CIE — an author-defined improvement over CIELAB
Polar form means hue arithmetic wraps at 360°, requiring mod operations

vs_hsl.advantage: Hue rotation actually looks uniform. Changing L changes brightness, not saturation. Triadic harmony at equal C looks actually equal.
vs_hsl.disadvantage: Harder to reason about raw values. Yellow is at h=109°, not 60°. Chroma C is not bounded like HSL saturation.
vs_hsl.recommendation: Use OKLCh for all creative color manipulation. Use HSL only for harmony angle math and final display mapping.

css_support.note: CSS Color Level 4. Supported in all modern browsers since 2023.

art_notes: OKLCh is the creative color space you've always wanted but didn't know existed. Spin the h dial and the hue changes uniformly. Pull the C slider and the color fades to gray without going greenish. Nudge L and the brightness changes cleanly. This is color as it actually works — not as HSL pretends it does. Use this for any interactive color picker or palette generator where you want results that look right, not results that are numerically tidy.
